connections.why: Knowing body systems underpins understanding training, diet and recovery
The skeletal and muscular systems provide the levers biomechanics analyses
Movement analysis combines physiological and biomechanical principles
How skills are learned connects to the psychology of performance
Psychological factors interact with the social context of sport
Physiological understanding informs effective practical performance
Biomechanical principles explain efficient technique in performance
Theories of skill development are applied when performing or coaching
Managing arousal and motivation supports performance under pressure
Performance must be carried out before its strengths and weaknesses can be analysed
Physiological knowledge helps diagnose fitness-related weaknesses
Understanding skill learning helps identify technical weaknesses
The analysis of weaknesses sets the targets the development programme addresses
Training principles are applied when designing the development programme
Practice and feedback methods shape how the programme develops skills
Goal setting and motivation strategies support the development programme
